title: Deciphering the dirty tanker record rally
section_path: Deciphering the dirty tanker record rally
section_path_text: Deciphering the dirty tanker record rally
summary:
Main
In this piece, we are revisiting the undisrupted rally of VLCC freight rates, as earnings broke the 1 million USD per day barrier. By Ioannis Papadimitriou
In order to decipher this historic level of freight rates we will focus on the drivers in three different parts:

1 - Cargo supply and demand
This is the perspective where record VLCC rates are least justified. Global crude departures have been around 44mbd over the last 2.5 months, about 5mbd lower than over the six months before the war started.

children.title: 1 - Cargo supply and demand
children.summary: This is the perspective where record VLCC rates are least justified. Global crude departures have been around 44mbd over the last 2.5 months, about 5mbd lower than over the six months before the war started.

children.title: 2 - Logistics and risk
children.summary: Probably a theme that has been repeated endlessly in 2026 and even before (Hormuz, wider Gulf regions, Red Sea, Black Sea for smaller crude tankers) but definitely one of the key driving factors throughout. The freight rate to shuttle oil from East to West of Hormuz is quoted around 75$/t which is roughly the difference between a West of Hormuz and East of Hormuz VLCC freight rates .

children.title: 3 - Vessel supply and demand
children.summary:
This is currently surely the most bullish element, and likely the main booster behind record freight rates. There are various factors that are constraining in particular vessel supply, including
a much higher concentration of the fleet after the Sinokor buying spree early in the year
the efforts to compile a fleet by regional MEG suppliers as well as by trading houses
Vessel positioning causing a supply-demand imbalance.
